Let the side length of each large square be \(2\), so each square has area \(4\).

### Figure I
The inner diamond has diagonals of length \(2\), so its area is
\[
\frac{2\cdot 2}{2}=2.
\]
Its side midpoints form the inner square, whose side length is \(1\), so its area is \(1\). Thus
\[
S_I=2-1=1=\frac14(4).
\]

### Figure II
Using coordinates, the triangle has vertices
\[
(0,0),\quad (1,2),\quad (2,1).
\]
Therefore its area is
\[
S_{II}=\frac12\left|\det
\begin{pmatrix}
1&2\\
2&1
\end{pmatrix}\right|
=\frac12|1-4|
=\frac32.
\]
The dashed line is a median dividing the shaded triangle into two equal parts.

### Figure III
The shaded triangle has base \(2\) and height \(2\), so
\[
S_{III}=\frac12(2)(2)=2.
\]

Thus
\[
1<\frac32<2,
\]
so
\[
\boxed{\text{B: }S_I<S_{II}<S_{III}}.
\]
